messages:
alex: FYI I opened a focused PR to tighten up the Dedicated SLA docs and add an operational checklist for fallback routing. Looking for docs + eng quick eyes before merging. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4310

maria: Thanks. Can you summarize the changes here? I might not get to the PR today.

alex: main changes:
- clarified SLA time buckets (p50/p95/p99) language for Dedicated pools
- added a short paragraph on tenant isolation expectations during fallback
- new working example showing a fallback_policy + compatibility guard + test checklist

sam: please paste the example here, easier to comment inline.

alex: pasted below:

```yaml
fallback_policy:
  - id: eu-fallback-on-latency
    trigger:
      metric: p99_latency_ms
      threshold: 150
    actions:
      - type: compatibility_check
        requires:
          - tool_calls
          - structured_outputs
      - type: route
        target: dedicated-eu-fallback
      - type: rate_limit
        limit: 10rps
      - type: degrade_model
        model: redwood/gpt-medium-quant
        note: "reduced context and no tool-call guarantees"
```

jin: couple suggestions: use explicit numeric units on threshold (ms) and clarify compatibility_check semantics. Maybe state it returns boolean and a reason.

harry: From runtime side: compatibility_check has to validate model capability and schema expectations. Also we should warn about KV cache mismatch on degrade_model — that can cause cold starts. Add a line in the checklist.

tara: docs nit: prefer prose that non-runtime readers can follow. Keep the YAML but also add a short paragraph describing what each step does in plain English.

alex: good calls. I'll make the threshold key `threshold_ms: 150` and add a comment about the compatibility_check boolean and reason. I'll also add a checklist entry about KV cache warmup and a recommended smoke test for tool-calls.

sam: suggest adding a sample telemetry label that should appear during fallback so customers can filter traces, e.g., `routing.fallback: eu-fallback-on-latency` and `model.variant: gpt-medium-quant`.

alex: adding telemetry labels to the checklist. Also adding an example curl-based smoke test to validate function-calls against the fallback model.

docs-bot: ran linter: docs/dedicated/sla-matrix.md: line 184: broken link to internal API reference.

alex: Thanks docs-bot, will fix link to /api/serving-routing instead of /api/routing.

jin: small suggestion on wording: avoid the term "degrade" in user-facing docs; maybe use "downgrade model variant" — less loaded.

tara: +1 on wording. Also add a short section that recommends how long to keep fallback telemetry retention for debugging (e.g., 72 hours).

alex: changed wording to "downgrade model variant" and added telemetry retention recommendation.

maria: I can review and approve tomorrow morning. Quick question: do we need a cross-ref to Dedicated capacity SLA PDF for sales?

harry: yes please add a brief note saying commercial SLA language may differ and link to the legal/enterprise SLA doc. Not a blocking doc change.

alex: will add a cross-ref and push update. If no major objections, I'll merge after the link fix and small wording changes.

sam: lgtm for content, not blocking.

jin: left a tiny grammar nit in the PR.

tara: wrote a short paragraph for the prose section, left in PR as suggested text.

alex: thanks everyone. I pushed the edits: fixed link, threshold_ms, wording, checklist with telemetry and KV cache item, and added the curl smoke test. Marking PR ready for merge unless further objections.

sam: lgtm

jin: left a tiny grammar nit in the PR.

tara: wrote a short paragraph for the prose section, left in PR as suggested text.

alex: thanks everyone. I pushed the edits: fixed link, threshold_ms, wording, checklist with telemetry and KV cache item, and added the curl smoke test. Marking PR ready for merge unless further objections.
